crossRefs.note: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?
crossRefs.keyword: vain words. Heb. words of wind

crossRefs.note: “How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?
crossRefs.keyword: vain words. Heb. words of wind

crossRefs.note: “Should a wise man answer with vain knowledge, and fill himself with the east wind?
crossRefs.keyword: vain words. Heb. words of wind

crossRefs.note: I have heard the reproof which puts me to shame. The spirit of my understanding answers me.
Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
No one was able to answer him a word, neither did any man dare ask him any more questions from that day forward.
whose mouths must be stopped: men who overthrow whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for dishonest…
and soundness of speech that can’t be condemned, that he who opposes you may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say…

translations.web: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?
translations.bsb: Is there no end to your long-winded speeches? What provokes you to continue testifying?
translations.kjv: Shall vain words have an end? or what emboldeneth thee that thou answerest?
translations.asv: Shall vain words have an end? Or what provoketh thee that thou answerest?
